title: Design System: Learn Anything — The Answer Sheet (Colour Press)

print-ink.note: Maps to --primary. The structure ink: ink-block CTAs, filled (completed) bubbles, wordmark, walked rail connectors, caret, selection. Night-desk rendition inverts this role to paper ink #f2e8d8 on ground #17131f.

engage-blue.note: Maps to --engage (text --on-engage #fffaf0; --ring is this blue in both themes). Touches ONLY activity and interaction: focus rings, current/active bubbles, working+executing stamps, active nav tab, the REVEAL outline control, option hover, the intake sheet's open-field focus and option-row hover, markdown links. Night desk: #4299f0 (#0b141e text). Never static or structural color, and never a plan number.

riso-pink-red.note: Maps to --error. The press's correction ink, re-pressed as riso. Reserved for misses, corrections, reveals, and the red sheet number only. Never success, never an inquiry identity. Night desk: #f5578d.

correction-field.note: Maps to --error-container. Background behind struck/missed answers and verdict panels. Night desk: #4b1027.

riso-green.note: Maps to --tertiary. Reserved strictly for verified/passed outcomes: the complete stamp, the correct option after a reveal, verdict lines. Never a confidence rung, never an inquiry identity. Night desk: #3fc578.

verified-field.note: Maps to --tertiary-container. Background behind verified/correct marks. Night desk: #143821.

pencil.note: Maps to --secondary. Meta/pending graphite voice; the mid rung of the confidence scale. Night desk: #a89b8a.

pencil-meta.note: Maps to --on-surface-variant. Meta copy, timestamps, unreached labels. Night desk: #b6ab9d.

press-paper.note: Maps to --background. Warm press-stock page ground, never pure white. Night desk: #17131f.

paper-white.note: Maps to --surface-container-lowest / --on-primary. The sheet itself: cards, option boxes, chips. Night desk: #100c17.

sheet-stock.note: Maps to --surface-container-low. Recessed form furniture: rail strip, dialog footers. Night desk: #1d1727.

rule.note: Maps to --outline-variant. Borders, ruled-paper lines, double rules, dashed ahead-connectors. Night desk: #453c55.

rule-strong.note: Maps to --outline. Stronger printed rules, quote borders, neutral verdict top rule. Night desk: #9a8fa0.

inq-blue.note: Maps to --inq-blue. One of the four inquiry identity inks (inquiryInk in lib/utils.ts, deterministic per session). Prints on sheet-card edges and sidebar step blocks only. Night desk: #58a6ff.

inq-flame.note: Maps to --inq-flame. Inquiry identity ink. Distinct hue family from the correction pink-red. Night desk: #ff8a4d.

inq-violet.note: Maps to --inq-violet. Inquiry identity ink. Night desk: #b39aff.

inq-ochre.note: Maps to --inq-ochre. Inquiry identity ink — the deep print of the highlighter family. Night desk: #e8b95c.

ink-on-spot.note: Maps to --on-inq. Text/fill on an inquiry spot block; flips to #17131f on the night desk's fluorescent spots.

highlighter-wash.note: The --marker pigment: riso yellow. Applied only as a translucent wash (48% light / 32% night desk) on the narrowed-goal line the app echoes back onto the Session intake sheet. Bounded exception; nothing else may use it.

display.purpose: The record header band title (History, Explore) and the Session intake sheet's pinned masthead ("START NEW SESSION"): Archivo 700 uppercase, widened tracking, closed by a double rule. The record band takes the rung at 30px; the intake masthead takes it at 20px with +0.06em tracking, exactly as that sheet shipped before the redesign (#204).

title.purpose: Sheet card goal titles, quiz prompts, session workspace header line - Archivo 600 at 20px. On the Session intake sheet the 20px rung is taken by the pinned masthead instead, in the display face at 700, uppercase, +0.06em; the sheet's own copy starts one rung below it, at Body.

body.purpose: All teaching copy, option text, plan steps, and the words the learner wrote; plain Source Sans 3 at 15px (600 where a line heads a field or a plan step), legible at any age, never uppercase. It is the only voice the Session intake sheet uses below its rail.

meta.purpose: The 14px annotation rung: field labels, in-flight notes, error lines, verdict captions, probe explanations, the plan's 'Builds on:' line, status-panel notes. Pencil meta by default, the role ink when the line reports a verdict. Labels and verdicts take the 600 weight; single-line meta closes to a 1.43 leading, reading notes stay at 1.71. Never uppercase, never monospace.

label.purpose: Monospace uppercase caps: stamps, rail step names, nav tabs, REVEAL, AGAIN/HARD/GOOD/EASY, verdict lines, and the form keys on the sign-in and regenerate-slide sheets. The rail's step names are this rung and are live on the intake sheet's rail; below the sm breakpoint only the current step's name is printed. The intake sheet's field labels, below that rail, are meta in the body face instead.

code.purpose: Monospace data: red sheet numbers, zero-padded counters, timestamps, batch positions.

shadows.name: sheet (night desk)
shadows.value: 0 1px 0 color-mix(in oklab, #453c55 80%, transparent), 0 2px 5px -2px color-mix(in oklab, #000 45%, transparent)
shadows.purpose: --shadow-sheet at rest: the sheet's edge contact on the desk.

shadows.name: sheet (riso paper)
shadows.value: 0 1px 0 color-mix(in oklab, #d3c6b0 90%, transparent), 0 2px 5px -2px color-mix(in oklab, #181420 22%, transparent)
shadows.purpose: --shadow-sheet on paper: 1px edge line plus a tight ink-tinted drop.

shadows.name: sheet-raised (night desk)
shadows.value: 0 2px 0 color-mix(in oklab, #453c55 90%, transparent), 0 8px 18px -6px color-mix(in oklab, #000 55%, transparent)
shadows.purpose: --shadow-sheet-raised hover/attention state, paired with a -1px translate. The only second level.

shadows.name: stamp inner rule
shadows.purpose: The inner border of a real stamp's double outline, tinted from the stamp's own ink; 2px inset on the 96px completion stamp.

shadows.name: halftone screen
shadows.purpose: The press's dot screen (the halftone utility). Printed in exactly two places: behind the record header band's CTA end (engage blue, 13%, md and up) and beside the login wordmark (blue, 25%). A signature accent, not required decoration.

motion.name: ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: The single easing shared by every authored moment; exponential ease-out from an already-visible default.

motion.name: bubble-fill
motion.purpose: A progress bubble inks in (scale 0.5→1, opacity 0.4→1). Quiz answers and rail steps.

motion.name: stamp-press
motion.purpose: A stamp settles from scale 1.08 / rotate -4° / 1px blur to rest at rotate -2°.

motion.name: sheet-settle
motion.purpose: A sheet card lands on the desk (6px rise); list cards stagger 40ms apart, capped at 320ms.

motion.name: pen-draw
motion.purpose: The red-pen cross: two hand-drawn pathLength strokes, never an icon dash trick.

motion.name: dot-breathe
motion.purpose: The breathing engagement-blue dot inside a current bubble.

motion.name: reduced-motion guard
motion.purpose: Every authored animation is switched off; the flow never depends on motion to be understood.

motion.name: plain-form surface motion
motion.value: shared dialog open 100ms (fade-in + zoom-in-95); 150ms colour transitions on option rows and fields; the ink block's 1px lift to --shadow-sheet-raised; animate-spin while a request is in flight
motion.purpose: What the Session intake sheet does below its rail. The press motions belong to the pinned band only: bubble-fill and dot-breathe appear on the rail's bubbles and nowhere else on the sheet, and no stamp-press, sheet-settle or pen-draw appears on it at all.

components.name: Ink Block Button
components.description: The page's single heavy primary CTA — a solid print-ink block resting at sheet contact, lifting one step on hover.

components.name: Reveal Control (outline stamp)
components.description: A hard 3px outline-stamp control with monospace caps, printed in engagement blue because revealing is interaction; hover fills blue with paper text.

components.name: Confidence Controls (AGAIN / HARD / GOOD / EASY)
components.description: The graded scale chips: a 3px top rule carries the rung (riso pink-red lapse → pencil → ink container → filled ink); no green appears in the scale. Hover adopts the rung color. Disabled while a recording is in flight.
components.css: .ds-confidence-row { display: flex; gap: 8px; } .ds-confidence { position: relative; overflow: hidden; background: var(--surface-container-lowest, #fffaf0); color: var(--on-surface, #181420); border: 1px solid var(--outline-variant, #d3c6b0); border-radius: 3px; padding: 8px 16px; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 700; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.12em; transition: all 150ms; } .ds-confidence .ds-rule { position: absolute; inset: 0 0 auto 0; height: 3px; } .ds-is-again .ds-rule { background: var(--error, #c81e5b); } .ds-is-hard .ds-rule { background: var(--secondary, #5f5643); } .ds-is-good .ds-rule { background: var(--primary-container, #2a2430); } .ds-is-easy .ds-rule { background: var(--primary, #181420); } .ds-is-again:hover { border-color: var(--error, #c81e5b); color: var(--error, #c81e5b); } .ds-is-hard:hover { border-color: var(--secondary, #5f5643); color: var(--on-surface, #181420); } .ds-is-good:hover { border-color: var(--primary, #181420); color: var(--primary, #181420); } .ds-is-easy:hover { background: var(--primary, #181420); color: var(--primary-foreground, #fffaf0); } .ds-confidence:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--ring, #1450a3); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-confidence:disabled { opacity: 0.5; }

components.name: Quiz Option Box
components.description: A printed lettered option on the surfaces that print questions (quiz cards, the review deck); hover shifts the border to engagement blue (the interaction ink). Revealed states: correct marked green, wrong pick struck with the red-pen cross. The intake sheet's boundary checks use plain Intake Option Rows instead - both treatments are current.
components.css: .ds-options { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 8px; } .ds-option { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; width: 100%; text-align: left; background: var(--surface-container-lowest, #fffaf0); color: var(--on-surface, #181420); border: 1px solid var(--outline-variant, #d3c6b0); border-radius: 4px; padding: 12px 16px; transition: border-color 150ms; } .ds-option:hover { border-color: var(--engage, #1450a3); } .ds-option:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--ring, #1450a3); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-text { flex: 1; font-family: 'Source Sans 3', sans-serif; font-size: 15px; } .ds-letter { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 28px; height: 28px; border: 1px solid var(--outline-variant, #d3c6b0); border-radius: 3px; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 700; color: var(--on-surface-variant, #4d4438); } .ds-reveal-correct { border-color: color-mix(in oklab, var(--tertiary, #167a3f) 60%, transparent); background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--tertiary-container, #c9e8d2) 50%, transparent); color: var(--tertiary, #167a3f); } .ds-letter-correct { border-color: var(--tertiary, #167a3f); background: var(--tertiary, #167a3f); color: var(--on-tertiary, #fffaf0); } .ds-reveal-wrong { border-color: color-mix(in oklab, var(--error, #c81e5b) 60%, transparent); background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--error-container, #f9dbe4) 40%, transparent); color: var(--error, #c81e5b); } .ds-letter-wrong { border-color: var(--error, #c81e5b); background: var(--error, #c81e5b); color: var(--on-error, #fffaf0); }

components.name: Intake Answer Field (recorded, and open ask)
components.description: The Session intake sheet's two states in one frame: an answer already recorded sits in a filled paper container under its 14px label; the one thing still being asked sits in the same family of field with the question itself as its label. Both states are the same width: the measure lives on the column, never on the item. Sentence-case body type throughout - no caps, no monospace - which is the rule below the sheet's rail; the pinned masthead and rail band above it are printed chrome.

components.name: Intake Option Row (open choice)
components.description: A boundary check on the plain form: outlined rows at the sheet's single measure, no letter square and no leading marker - the row is the control, and pressing it is the answer. A blue border on hover/focus is the only signal it gives.
components.css: .ds-intake-rows { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 8px; max-width: 480px; } .ds-intake-row { width: 100%; text-align: left; background: transparent; color: var(--on-surface, #181420); border: 1px solid var(--outline-variant, #d3c6b0); border-radius: 4px; padding: 12px 16px; font-family: 'Source Sans 3', sans-serif; font-size: 15px; line-height: 24px; transition: border-color 150ms; } .ds-intake-row:hover { border-color: var(--engage, #1450a3); } .ds-intake-row:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--ring, #1450a3); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-intake-row:disabled { opacity: 0.6; }

components.name: Intake Milestone Panel (a phase ends)
components.description: The one block on the Session intake sheet's record that is not a field: it states that a phase the learner worked through has ended. The same filled container the sheet closes on - paper fill, 1px rule, 4px cut, 16px padding - with the Check in verified green and the sentence in ink at 15px, and its action at the panel's right end. Its copy names what the learner did and how far they got, never the core's phase vocabulary (#204).
components.html: ✓You've answered 12 questions to get here. Now we know where your understanding starts - your learning plan is ready.
components.css: .ds-intake-milestone { max-width: 480px; background: var(--surface-container-lowest, #fffaf0); border: 1px solid var(--outline-variant, #d3c6b0); border-radius: 4px; padding: 16px; } .ds-intake-milestone-line { display: flex; align-items: flex-start; gap: 10px; font-family: 'Source Sans 3', sans-serif; font-size: 15px; line-height: 24px; color: var(--on-surface, #181420); } .ds-intake-milestone-line .ds-check { margin-top: 2px; font-size: 16px; color: var(--tertiary, #167a3f); } .ds-intake-actions { margin-top: 12px; display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center; justify-content: flex-end; gap: 8px; } .ds-btn-ink { background: var(--primary, #181420); color: var(--on-primary, #fffaf0); border: 0; border-radius: 6px; padding: 10px 16px; font-family: 'Source Sans 3', sans-serif; font-size: 15px; }

components.name: Sheet Card (History / Review deck)
components.description: A filed answer sheet: the inquiry's identity spot as a 5px press edge on the left, punch-hole margin, ruled header strip with a red monospace sheet number, title below. Carries no stage vocabulary (product decision #46).

components.name: Progress Rail & Bubbles
components.description: The sole progress device, live on the Session intake sheet directly under the pinned masthead: a printed row of four bubbles and mono-caps step names; done steps join with a solid ink rule, ahead steps with a dashed rule. Bubbles: empty, filled (ink), current (blue ring + breathing blue dot), active (filled blue). The element is the sheet's role=status and its counter is an aria-label only, never printed. Below sm (640px) every step name except the current one is sr-only.

narrative.overview:
Study is a sheet you fill in. Every surface is printed paper: a record header closed by a double rule, sessions as paper cards punched for a binder, questions as lettered option boxes, progress as a row of filled bubbles, phase as a rotated rubber stamp pressed onto the page. The system holds to a colour press — ink-black carries the structure, engagement blue marks activity, riso pink-red corrects, riso green verifies, pencil annotates, and every inquiry is printed in its own spot color, so the History reads as a color-coded map of what you are curious about — on a warm press-paper ground with a faint grain (3.5% opacity) that says "sheet", not "panel".

Since 2026-10-18 the "sheet you fill in" is drawn literally on one surface: the Session intake is a plain form on that same ground — one column of labelled items, the record of what was asked and answered kept on the sheet itself, the one open ask below it, filled containers for answers and outlined full-width rows for open choices. Below its rail it borrows none of the printed-form devices, and the palette was pinned at the same time: a redesign may replace type, geometry, material, composition and motion but never re-colour the app. Above the rail is the band the owner pinned (#204), and that band prints: a display-face masthead and the world's own progress track of bubbles and mono-caps step names. Everything else still prints too: record headers, filed cards, lettered option boxes, stamps and bubbles. Both idioms draw their colour roles, depth, and type ramp from the same tokens.

The world ships in two complete renditions: riso paper (light) and the night desk (dark, the same press inverted with glowing inks on a warm desk). No role changes meaning between them. The color system was replaced on 2026-10-02 by the owner's chosen "Colour Press" direction; every non-color rule of the Answer Sheet world carried forward into it.

Type carries the printed-form logic on the record surfaces: Archivo sets record headers like a printed masthead; Source Sans 3 is the plain body voice legible at any age; JetBrains Mono is the record's own hand — codes, counters, and the caps pressed into stamps, controls, and the rail's step names. The Session intake sheet splits at its rail, and only there: its pinned masthead is the display face and its step names are monospace caps, while everything the learner reads and fills in below the rail is one body face on the 15/14 ramp, sentence case.
keyCharacteristics: Colour-press discipline: ink structures; engagement blue touches only activity and interaction; pink-red corrects; green verifies; pencil annotates; inquiry spots identify.
Every inquiry carries a deterministic identity spot (blue / flame / violet / ochre) on its sheet edge and sidebar step blocks — History reads as a color-coded map of curiosities.

Bubbles are the sole progress device — empty, filled (ink), current (blue ring + breathing blue dot), or active (filled blue). No progress bars. On the Session intake sheet the rail is where position is stated, and it is stated once.
Stamps (slightly rotated, double-ruled, monospace caps) are the phase vocabulary on the live session workspace; session cards carry no stage vocabulary at all (product decision #46).

Square-cut form geometry: form surfaces at or below 6px radius; full circles reserved for bubbles and punch holes. The intake sheet has no silhouette of its own — full-bleed, fields and rows cut at 4px.
Ruled-paper writing areas, double-rule dividers, punch-hole margins, a ruled meta strip with a red monospace "No." on every filed card, and the halftone dot screen as a signature accent.

Two form idioms, cleanly separated: record surfaces print like a form (Archivo caps, monospace keys, ruled paper); the Session intake sheet is a plain form below its rail on 15/14 sentence-case body type. Neither idiom is banned — on the intake sheet the boundary between them is drawn inside the surface, at the rail.
No glow, no gradients, no glass. Depth is the contact shadow of paper on a desk, or one tonal step between ground and field on the plain form.

rules.name: The Colour Press Rule
rules.body: Every color in the app holds its reserved role: ink structures, the blue touches only activity and interaction, pink-red corrects, green verifies, pencil annotates, inquiry spots identify. A color that crosses its reservation is a bug, not a variant.

rules.name: The Identity Is Not a Verdict Rule
rules.body: The inquiry fan is exactly blue / flame / violet / ochre, assigned deterministically per session; it deliberately excludes the correction pink-red and the verified green. Identity is never a verdict.

rules.name: The Red Sheet Number Rule
rules.body: Every filed sheet — a history card, a review card, the empty sheet — prints its identity as a red monospace "No." on its ruled header strip. It is the card's fingerprint, not decoration.

rules.name: The Highlighter Exception
rules.body: --marker (riso yellow wash, 48% on paper / 32% on the night desk) is the one wash outside the press, bounded to the narrowed-goal line the app echoes back onto the Session intake sheet. A highlighter belongs on an answer sheet — but only on the learner's own answer.

rules.name: The Printed-Form Rule
rules.body: Headings are set like a printed form: Archivo, uppercase where it is a header band — a record band, or the Session intake sheet's pinned masthead — with widened tracking. The teaching voice itself is never uppercase and never the display face.

rules.name: The One Voice Per Sheet Rule
rules.body: A surface picks one label voice and uses it everywhere on that surface. The sign-in and regenerate-slide sheets print monospace form keys (11-12px caps, +0.12-0.14em). On the Session intake sheet the boundary runs at the rail: the pinned band above it is printed chrome — the display-face masthead and the rail's mono-caps step names — and everything the learner reads and fills in below it is the body face on the 15px reading / 14px label-and-meta ramp, sentence case, no caps and no monospace below that line except the counters the rail itself prints. What decides which voice a band gets is what that band asks of the reader.

rules.name: The Mono-Vocabulary Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono is the record's hand: codes and counters per the brief, extended by the build to FORM labels — the caps on stamps, nav tabs, the sign-in fields, the REVEAL / AGAIN / HARD / GOOD / EASY controls, and the rail's step names. Mono never sets body copy or teaching prose, and the intake sheet's field labels below its rail are meta in the body face, not form keys.

rules.name: The Sheet-Contact Rule
rules.body: Every lifted thing shows its edge. A shadow is always a contact line plus a tight drop; anything diffuse, wide, or colored is outside this world. A surface that lifts nothing — the plain form — says so with tone instead, and takes no shadow to look like it has depth.

rules.name: The One Ink Block Rule
rules.body: Each page or sheet carries exactly one heavy solid-ink primary CTA; everything else is an outline, a chip, or a plain link. It is set in the body face at 15px, sentence case — the ink block is a sentence, not a form key.

rules.name: The One State Device Rule
rules.body: On the intake form — every field and row below its rail — a container's fill is its state, and it is the only state device that part of the sheet has: filled paper means the answer is already recorded; an outlined full-width row means the choice is still open. Nothing else marks state there — no leading marker, no check, no ring. A circle that never fills promises a selection state the row does not have. The row of bubbles above it is a progress device under a different rule: it says where the learner is, never whether a field is answered.

rules.name: The Bubble-Only Progress Rule
rules.body: Where the system draws progress it is a row of bubbles in four states only — empty, filled, current, active. There are no bars, rings, or percentage meters, and there is no second device beside them: the Session intake sheet states position on its rail and nowhere else — never a sentence under the title, never a count repeated inside the field the rail has already numbered. A surface with no rail says where the reader stands in words; a surface that prints the rail prints the rail.

dos: Do keep every color inside its press role: ink structures, the engagement blue only marks activity and interaction (focus, current, running, active nav, reveal, an open row's hover), pink-red only corrects, green only verifies, pencil only annotates.
Do give each inquiry its spot from inquiryInk and use it only as identity — sheet-card edge and sidebar step blocks.
Do mark progress with bubbles only — empty, filled, current, active — and connect walked steps with solid ink rules, ahead steps with dashed ones.
Do set phase as a stamp: rotated -2 degrees, double-outlined, monospace caps, pressed in; blue while working, green when complete, pink-red on error.

Do file every filed card the same way — history, review, and empty-state cards: punch-hole margin, ruled header strip, red monospace "No.", 6px corners, sheet-contact shadow. The intake sheet is not a filed card; it is the sheet being filled.

Do run the part of a surface the learner fills in as a plain form: one column with its measure stated once at the column (the Session intake sheet: 32rem padded 16px, so every item on it is 30rem and no item carries a width of its own), 15px reading text with a 14px label-and-meta rung, sentence case, actions at the right end of the item they belong to.

Do keep the Session intake sheet's pinned header band exactly as it is (#204): the display-face masthead closed with the double rule, and the four-step rail straight beneath it. Position belongs to that rail — one statement, in its aria-label and its counters.

Do keep the filled-versus-outlined distinction as the only state device on a form sheet: filled paper (--surface-container-lowest, 1px rule) for what is already recorded, an outlined full-width row for what is still waiting to be pressed.

Do name progress for assistive technology in the element that draws it: the rail's counter is its aria-label ("3 steps to your lesson" → "Approve to build your lesson" → "Your lesson is on the way") and is never printed as a second line.
Do give each page or sheet exactly one ink block — the heavy solid-ink primary CTA — and set it in the body face at 15px, sentence case.
Do use the highlighter wash (--marker) on the learner's own narrowed goal on the intake sheet, and there only.

Do keep type legible at any age in both scripts: Source Sans 3 body at 15px with the 14px meta rung beneath it, uppercase Archivo only for record header bands, mono only for codes, counters, and form keys on the surfaces that print in that voice.
Do ship every surface in both renditions — riso paper and night desk — from the same role tokens, fields kept one step above the ground.
donts: Don't use pink-red on anything that succeeded, or green on anything unverified (including the confidence scale).
Don't assign the correction pink-red or the verified green as an inquiry identity spot; the fan is blue / flame / violet / ochre.
Don't use the engagement blue on anything static or structural — headings, sheet bodies, completed bubbles, plan numbers stay out of it.
Don't put stage or phase vocabulary on session cards (product decision #46).

Don't dress the part of the Session intake sheet below its rail in the record devices: ruled paper, stamps, lettered option boxes, monospace caps, the display face, or left-ruled chat bubbles. Each stays native to the surfaces that still use it — and the pinned header band above the rail is one of them (#204).

Don't put a meter anywhere, and don't state position twice: on a sheet that prints the rail, the rail states it once — not a sentence under the title, not a count inside the field it has already numbered. Don't put a marker on a row whose only state is 'press me'.
Don't round form surfaces past 8px; full circles are reserved for bubbles and punch holes.
Don't use glow, gradients, glass, or diffuse ambient shadows anywhere — depth is contact plus a tight drop, or one tonal step between ground and field.
Don't use progress bars, rings, or percentage meters; where the system draws progress, the bubble row is the device.
Don't treat LLM-authored slide content in the sandbox iframe as app chrome; the system frames it, never styles it from outside.
Don't invent a second highlighter, a second accent family, or a decorative color; the press has its quota.
